terms.label: Founder
terms.meaning: A person who brought a founding contribution to a venture at its founding, has a stake in it, and shows up in its record. A venture may have several.

properties.says: a person, or an entity whose owners trace to people
there before the first hire, investment or paying customer
brought a founding contribution, evidenced in provenance
has a stake: equity or a signed founder agreement
shows up in provenance through decisions or work

sources: Paul Graham, The 18 Mistakes That Kill Startups (2006)

terms.label: Co-founder
terms.meaning: A founder of a venture that has at least one other founder.

properties.says: a person, or an entity whose owners trace to people
there before the first hire, investment or paying customer
brought a founding contribution, evidenced in provenance
has a stake: equity or a signed founder agreement
shows up in provenance through decisions or work
another founder on the same venture

sources: Paul Graham, The 18 Mistakes That Kill Startups (2006)

terms.label: Early employee
terms.meaning: Someone with a stake and work in the venture who brought no idea, secret, ethos, mission or capital to its founding.

properties.says: a person
has a stake
shows up in provenance
brought no idea, secret, ethos, mission or capital

terms.label: Mentor
terms.meaning: Someone who has walked the path the other is on, helps the whole person over a long horizon under sacred trust, spends their own standing for them, and aims at their release.

properties.says: lived experience of the other's path, drawn on
whole-person, long horizon
sacred trust T1 to T5 hold
directive allowed (a permission, never fails)
spends standing for the other at least once
aims at release: dependence falls

terms.label: Coach
terms.meaning: Someone who, under an explicit agreement, helps the client reach the client's own goal mostly by asking, with an accountability loop and sacred trust.

properties.says: explicit agreement: goal, success, duration
elicitive: most turns are questions or reflections
process, not path (a permission, never fails)
commitments made and reviewed
the client owns the goal and actions
sacred trust T1 to T5 hold

terms.label: Friend
terms.meaning: Two people who each wish the other well for the other's own sake, know it, and share life over time, as peers. Kind (utility, pleasure, character) is a facet, not a test.

properties.says: goodwill for the other's sake, beyond exchange
mutual and known
time together: a shared history
not only under a contract
peers: neither holds authority by role

sources: Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics VIII-IX (from memory, to check)

terms.label: Unearned candour
terms.meaning: Advice or judgement offered as candour about another person's path, when the speaker lacks standing, context or consent. An act in one encounter, not a role.

properties.says: framed as candour
about the other's path
missing standing
missing context: no inquiry first
missing consent

terms.rule: U1 and U2, and any of U3, U4, U5
sources: Schaerer et al. 2018, Advice Giving: A Subtle Pathway to Power

terms.label: Threshold guardian
terms.meaning: Whoever or whatever stands where someone crosses into a new world and tests whether they are ready. A role relative to one crossing; need not be a person.

properties.says: at a crossing into a new world
tests or blocks, not helping outright
not the main opponent of the whole journey
passable without destroying it
the role ends once the crossing is made

terms.label: Phase gate
terms.meaning: The exit of a venture phase: it tests readiness through exit criteria, is passed by meeting them, and is not a person.

properties.says: at a crossing into a new world
tests or blocks, not helping outright
not the main opponent of the whole journey
passable without destroying it
the role ends once the crossing is made
the crossing is a phase exit
not a person
